# Claim-wait cost: passes, broadcasts and wall-time attribution

When reviewing event-driven waits, price full claim passes separately from broadcast receives. A live subscription attaches before the first claim, receives/clones every Event, then filters its kind and seat. Unrelated events need not trigger SQL but still cost receiver polling and String/payload cloning. Scaling is waiters multiplied by total event rate, and copying scales with total payload bytes as well.

`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:2291-2299` holds `HeldSpan` across `subscription.next()`. `crates/daemon/src/http/route_counts.rs:99-140` subtracts that span's entire wall duration. Consequently inbox active_us excludes filtering/clone CPU executed inside the wait. A route-cost improvement is not by itself proof of lower daemon CPU or proof that broadcast work is cheap. Pair process CPU deltas with event throughput; never infer CPU shares from subscriber wake counts.

`Queue::next_claimable_in` adds a schema-version PRAGMA as well as the MIN query. "One indexed read per empty pass" is not "one SQLite statement." An indexed MIN can still visit every matching live row; distinguish kind/state isolation from constant-time backlog cost.

At #310's exact head 92787c46d0fef581b36fe93e426d90b671f502a1, the undisturbed 55 s native wait makes four passes, with no final deadline pass. The CI pass-count test counts two initial recipient reads and two reads per pass: six in 20 s. Endpoint completion counters do not measure these inner passes.

Receipts: performance verdict on pr:310; Rust CI run 44867815618, successful job 136735344617, artifact 14691978813, twelve focused regressions passed. Its live window was BEFORE only and included other fleet activity; no deployed improvement was claimed. Machine spawn-rate sampling ran separately from CPU sampling because that busy poll adds observer overhead.

**magicWand:** one read-only cost-window command pairing route/CPU/spawn evidence and exposing inner-pass/subscriber-receive counters.

**difficulties:** missing node_modules in the detached review worktree correctly limited TS proof to exact-head CI (C25). The quick gate also picked up an incompatible ambient Biome, demonstrating why global-tool fallback is not locked-toolchain evidence. Copilot memory voting was unavailable; role memory remains written through the governed CLI. Local quick-check availability is reported separately from product CI, never disguised as a green local gate.
